artworks.title: Forked-tail Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a print of a bird perched on a branch with its back to us, surrounded by blooming white flowers. The bird has a long, forked tail and a mix of blue and black plumage, accented with a hint of yellow on its crown and white on its legs and throat. The bird's brown eye is wide open as it looks upward and to the left. The thin brown branch has several white flowers with yellow centers amidst green leaves and small buds. There is a line of text at the bottom of the print.

artworks.title: Mangrove Cuckoo
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a bird on a branch among green leaves and white flowers. The bird has vibrant plumage blending shades of orange and brown, with a long tail marked with black and white patterns. Its wings exhibit a mix of gray and brown hues. The bird is perched on a slender branch among large, lush green leaves, rich in detail with various shades of green and intricate vein patterns. Delicate white flowers with orange centers add contrast to the scene. The composition emphasizes naturalistic elements, capturing the bird and surrounding flora with lifelike precision.

artworks.title: Gray Tyrant
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a gray bird perched on a branch with vibrant red and white flowers and green leaves. The bird, identified as a Gray Tyrant, Tyrannus Griseus, is depicted with remarkable detail, showcasing its soft gray plumage and striking red marking on its head. The surrounding flora consists of elegantly curve-tipped flowers in shades of deep red to crimson, with delicate green tendrils and leaves that provide a lush background.

artworks.title: Barn Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is print of two barn owls perched on the branches of a leafless tree against a dark sky, with a landscape of a distant river lined with trees visible below. The owl at the top of the painting has its wings spread, and it holds a small brown chipmunk in one claw, gripping the creature's head. The other owl is on a lower branch, and it has its wings partially raised and its beak is open, looking up towards the chipmunk held by the other owl. The feather patterns on both birds are detailed, showing the white on their faces, underbellies, and beneath their wings, as well as the warm brown tones of their heads, backs, and wings. The sky behind them is dark blue-gray.

artworks.title: Blue-headed Pigeon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Three birds on a rocky surface surrounded by grass and plants. The birds have vibrant blue heads, brown bodies, and some black and white markings. The color palette includes earthy browns, bright blue, rich greens, and pale oranges and reds in the background flora. Two birds are on the lower left, one facing right and the other slightly behind. The third bird is on the right side of the image, standing tall on a rock. Green blades of grass and orange flowers are primarily on the right, with a lighter background representing the sky.

artworks.title: Barn Swallow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two swallows perched on a nest. The birds are depicted with rich coloring, showcasing their blue feathers and reddish-brown underparts. The nest is crafted from mud and straw, creating intricate texture. The background is minimal, accentuating the focus on the swallows and their nest. This composition highlights the beauty of the birds and their nesting environment. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Olive-sided Flycatcher
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds are perched on a pine branch with blue-grey pine cones. The birds are gray and brown with white undersides. The color palette includes brown, gray, white, green, and dark blue. One bird is upright on the top left branch, while the other is mid-flight or perched vertically with its head pointing downward on the lower right branch.

artworks.title: Nuttall's Lesser Marsh Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a nest surrounded by tall grass. The painting features two small brown birds situated on a intricately woven nest that is nestled within dense, verdant grass. The birds have detailed plumage with varying shades of brown and are depicted with realistic attention to their feathers and posture. The nest is shown as a carefully crafted bundle of twigs and grass, set amidst tall, slender green blades that fill the composition. The background is left plain, emphasizing the intricacy and realism of the nest and birds.

artworks.title: Spotted Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of four birds in a natural setting. The birds are known as "Spotted Grouse" and are portrayed on a grassy and vegetative terrain. They are depicted with detailed brown, black, and white plumage with red accents near their heads. The birds are surrounded by lush green leaves and red berries. The artwork conveys a sense of serenity and harmony, reflecting the birds in their natural habitat. The style of the painting is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White-crowned Pigeon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two white-crowned pigeons among vibrant foliage and flowers. The pigeons are surrounded by lush green leaves and striking orange-red flowers. Each bird has a white cap on its head and deep blue plumage. The painting captures the birds' delicate features and dynamic pose. The scene is filled with vivid colors from the birds' habitat. The style of the painting resembles that of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Orange-crowned Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two small birds perched on a flowering plant. The birds have olive-green plumage and are surrounded by slender branches with pink blossoms and green leaves. The painting aims to capture the natural beauty of the birds and foliage with fine lines and soft coloration in a serene composition. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed illustrations of birds and their habitats.

artworks.title: Wood Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a Wood Wren perched on the ground surrounded by plants and berries in earthy tones, including greens, browns, reds, and blues. The bird is positioned on the left side of the image, with green leaves and blue berries on the right, and some red berries nearby.

artworks.title: Pine Finch
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a conifer branch. The painting depicts two small birds with speckled brown plumage interacting with the pine tree, which is adorned with green needles and small cones. The birds are depicted with one facing towards the cones and the other facing the opposite direction. The detailed and realistic rendering of both the birds and the tree branch highlights the precision and love for ornithological detail typical of Audubon's work. The plain background enhances the focus on the naturalistic portrayal of the birds and their surroundings.

artworks.title: Golden Eagle
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a golden eagle carrying a hare. The painting depicts a golden eagle in flight, holding a white hare in its talons against a sky backdrop. The eagle's feathers are detailed, showcasing browns and golds. The hare appears lifeless. The background features a rocky landscape with mountains in the distance.

artworks.title: Ground Dove
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows several doves perched on a green branch. Brown and white doves are resting among the branches and leaves of a tree with green fruits hanging from the branches. The birds are detailed with subtle color gradations, primarily brown and olive tones in their feathers, showcasing various profiles and postures. The leaves show veins and texture, enhancing the realism of the scene in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Golden-Crested Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two small birds are perched on a plant with elongated leaves and clustered flowers. One bird is facing upwards and the other is facing downwards. The background is off-white, contrasting with the vibrant colors of the birds and the plant.

artworks.title: Mangrove Humming Bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows multiple hummingbirds feeding on bright orange flowers on a vine. The birds are predominantly green with touches of pink and red. The vine runs vertically in the center, with flowers facing different directions. The hummingbirds are positioned throughout the image interacting with the flowers.

artworks.title: Bachman's Warbler
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image features two birds with yellow and gray plumage perched on a branch surrounded by lush green leaves and white flowers with bright yellow centers. The color palette includes vibrant greens and yellows alongside the neutral tones of the birds and the white of the flowers. The top bird is located towards the left side of the image, on a branch above the flowers, while the second bird is positioned near the bottom right, amidst the greenery and closer to the flowers.

artworks.title: Pinnated Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of birds and flowers in a natural setting. In the artwork, three birds are depicted with vibrant colors and detail. One bird is in flight with its wings spread wide, showcasing intricate feather patterns ranging from browns to grays. The other two birds are on the ground, potentially engaging in a social behavior. Nearby, a cluster of bright yellow flowers with elongated petals adds a burst of color against a green background. In the distance, rolling hills and mountains are visible. This painting is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Boat-tailed Grackle
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Two birds are perched on a branch surrounded by greenery. One bird is a Boat-tailed Grackle displaying iridescent blue and black plumage, while the other bird is brown. The foliage consists of green leaves with some small brown patches. The birds are positioned near the center of the image, with one facing left on a lower branch and the other facing left on a higher branch. Acorns are visible among the leaves.

artworks.title: Tree Sparrow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two sparrows perched on a branch with red berries. The artwork features two sparrows depicted on a branch with multicolored leaves. The birds are shown with detailed plumage, one positioned above the other, interacting with their natural surroundings. The composition highlights the elegance and delicate balance of nature, capturing a moment of these birds amidst a backdrop of abundant foliage. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Snow Bunting
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three snow buntings. The largest one is flying at the top, displaying its white, black, and brown patterned wings. The birds are predominantly brown, white, and black, set against a natural background of hills and foliage. The flying bird is at the top, with the other two on the ground, one looking up and one resting in greenery. The background features mountains under a cloudy sky.

artworks.title: Yellow-bellied Woodpecker
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a drawing of two woodpeckers on a branch with leaves and berries. The image illustrates two yellow-bellied woodpeckers perched on a slender branch with green leaves and dark berries. One bird is upright, displaying black and white plumage with red patches on its head. The other woodpecker is hanging upside down, showing a tan and yellow underbelly. Below the composition are inscriptions of "Yellow-bellied Woodpecker" and scientific classification details.

artworks.title: Willow Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts two grouse birds with their chicks in a natural setting. One grouse stands on a mound of moss while the other shelters its chicks on a rocky surface. Various plants, including flowers and foliage, surround them. The birds are detailed with feather patterns and the environment is textured with greens and browns. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's realistic portrayal of birds in their habitats.
